previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 18th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with no significant side effects. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately, falling to 0.07 by discharge, with no renal toxicity. Liver enzymes showed mild, expected elevation. A brain MRI confirmed stable disease without lymphoma recurrence. Aspirin was held during admission to optimize methotrexate excretion and was restarted at discharge. She remained emotionally stable on citalopram with no depressive symptoms. Chronic right foot pain persisted and was managed with gabapentin and PRN oxycodone; she was advised to follow up with her primary care physician for further evaluation. She was discharged home in good condition with plans to start Rituxan in the upcoming cycle.

___ is a ___ woman with ulcerative colitis,

high-dose methotrexate. 

Cycle #1 was complicated by a LLE DVT and PE, treated with 6 
months of enoxaparin. Many cycles have been complicated by a 
mild transient transaminitis. She also has a burning right foot 
pain of unknown etiology radiating up the leg. This is still 
moderately severe limiting how much walking she can do. MRI 
spine, doppler ultrasound, and lumbar puncture were negative. 
Cycle #12 required transfer to in-patient Psychiatry for a 
suicide attempt by drug overdose prior to the admission. She now 
denies depression or suicidal ideation. States that at the time, 
she felt overwhelmed with the number of cycles of therapy. She 
is well controlled on citalopram. Cycle #16 was complicated by 
an ulcerative colitis flare with hematochezia. Colonoscopy 
___ showed mild proctitis. GI bleeding stopped with several 
days of PR mesalamine. She has not had any futher UC flares 
since that episode and does not currently take any controlling 
medications. She tolerated cycles #17 and #18 well without any 
complications aside from slight transaminase elevation.

Today, she feels well, no complaints. She has been feeling more 
tired over the past month. She started rituximab 2 weeks ago and 
is now alternating regimens with MTX and rituximab.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ is a ___ woman with ulcerative colitis, 
asthma, DVT/PE, and CNS lymphoma admitted for cycle #19 
high-dose methotrexate as monthly maintenance therapy.  

ACUTE ISSUES:
============
1. CNS Lymphoma: Patient admitted for cycle #19 of high-dose 
methotrexate. Tolerated chemotherapy well except for mild 
nausea. Urine alkalinization with sodium bicarbonate PO and IV 
fluids to enhance methotrexate excretion. N/V control with 
Ativan and compazine, held Zofran as patient does not tolerate 
well (headaches). Leucovorin rescue was started 24 hours after 
MTX given. MTX levels were followed daily, and she was 
discharged home when MTX 0.14 uM. Provided 3 days leucovorin and 
sodium bicarb on discharge.
 
CHRONIC ISSUES:
============
1. Ulcerative Colitis: GI consulted during her admission for 
cycle #17 given UC flare. She had a colonoscopy ___ at 
___ which showed mild proctitis, remainder of colon 
normal. She was switched from PO mesalamine to PR dosing and 
hematochezia resolved quickly. She has been off these 
medications since that time.  No mesalamine this admission.
  
2. Right Foot Pain/Right Leg Weakness: Chronic, unclear 
etiology. Continued outpatient gabapentin and PRN oxycodone.
  
3. Transaminase Elevation: Patient has history of mild 
transaminase elevation with each cycle of MTX. LFTs were 
monitored and LFTs remained stable this admission.

4. LLE DVT/PE: Patient stopped enoxaparin ___ and changed 
to aspirin per Neuro-oncologist Dr. ___. Held aspirin during 
admission to enhance MTX excretion, restarted at discharge. Pt 
received heparin SC for DVT prophylaxis.

5. Nasal Irritation:  Chronic, controlled.  Continued 
fluticasone nasal.

6. Anemia: Chemo-induced. Mild, stable.  Continued vitamin D.

7. Depression: Controlled. Continued outpatient citalopram, 
trazodone for sleep.  

8. Asthma: Chronic, controlled. Continued outpatient 
fluticasone/salmeterol, montelukast, albuterol and ipratroprium 
PRN 

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
=================
- Pt should take leucovorin and sodium bicarb for 3 days after 
discharge.
- Next MTX cycle in one month.
